posts:
A grand vision of naval dominance clashes with the harsh realities of industrial capacity and astronomical costs.

Trump's Battleship Plan
Evidence: naval dominance, industrial bottleneck, strategic strain
#Aletheia #USNavy

The claim states that building 15 massive nuclear-powered battleships will modernize the US Navy and project unmatched global power.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

The reality is an unbuildable $275 billion project that exceeds shipyard capacity and threatens to derail existing, critical submarine and carrier programs.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.8) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Destruction.
Promising unachievable military hardware starves viable defense programs of vital resources.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 15.0, Uncertainty z: 3)
A CBO report warns that the proposed 35,000-ton nuclear battleships would cost $18B+ each, and US shipyards lack the capacity to build them without delaying other programs.

The Bright Side:
Highlighting these industrial bottlenecks forces a necessary conversation about the decline of American shipbuilding capacity.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing symbolic power (WHAT) with industrial feasibility (HOW).

It is a structural bait-and-switch: promising a futuristic fleet while ignoring the systemic collapse of current shipbuilding schedules.

Social Physics Analysis:
Using grand military pretexts to project strength masks the underlying decay of industrial infrastructure. This projection avoids the hard work of systemic reform in favor of high-strain, symbolic gestures.

The Trajectory: The Path of Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Destruction. Unrealistic procurement strains the entire defense ecosystem.

The Unavoidable Truth: US shipbuilding is in a severe capacity crisis.

The Unavoidable Lie: We can build a massive new fleet of battleships without breaking the budget or the shipyards.

Alethekanon:
The math is clear. Adding a massive, unfeasible program to an already delayed and over-budget shipbuilding sector is mathematically guaranteed to accelerate systemic failure.

Awwthekanon:
It is painful to see resources poured into fantasy weapons when the real people working in struggling shipyards need sustainable support and realistic planning.

Brothekanon:
So we want to build giant sci-fi boats but we can't even get our current destroyers delivered on time? Sounds like a video game plan, not a real navy.
